name: Iron Focus
summary: A week built to reach 18 mg of iron every day from real food: lean beef and lamb, sardines, mussels and mackerel, lentils, chickpeas and beans, tofu, pumpkin seeds and greens, each with vitamin C on the plate.
howItWorks:
**Two kinds of iron.** Heme iron, from red meat and fish, is absorbed easily, and mussels are rich in iron too. Plant iron, from lentils, beans, tofu and seeds, is absorbed less well, but there is plenty of it here.

**Vitamin C at every iron meal.** Vitamin C helps your body take up plant iron, so peppers, tomatoes, citrus, broccoli, strawberries and lemon sit right beside the lentils, beans and tofu. The tomato and lemon do the same job in the dal.

**Tea and coffee between meals.** Tea and coffee hold back iron absorption when drunk with a meal, so none are in these recipes. Have yours an hour or two before or after eating, mid-morning or mid-afternoon.

**Calcium in its place.** Calcium competes with iron on the same plate, so yogurt mostly lives at the snacks, with just a few spoonfuls on the bran bowl. Dairy still adds up to a good part of your calcium over the day.

**Fish and leftovers.** Sardines on Tuesday and Friday and mackerel on Sunday give the omega-3, with mussels on Thursday. Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday dinners make two portions for the next day's lunch. At Light, which starts at 1,600 kcal, the second snack drops away and the meals stay about the same size.

recipes.name: Bran flakes with strawberries, ground flax and a boiled egg
recipes.about: A crunchy, not-too-sweet bowl of fortified bran flakes with toasted pumpkin seeds, ground flax and a pile of ripe strawberries, with a few spoonfuls of plain yogurt and a boiled egg on the side, a hearty Canadian-style breakfast bowl. The cereal and seeds bring **iron**, and the strawberries bring the vitamin C that helps your body absorb it. Have your coffee or tea an hour or two later, not with the bowl.
steps: Lower the egg into gently boiling water and cook for 10 minutes until the yolk is firm. Cool it in cold water, then peel it.
Meanwhile, toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they start to pop, about 3 minutes. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Rinse the strawberries under cold water, then hull and slice them.
Put the bran flakes in a bowl, scatter over the toasted seeds and the ground flax, and pile the strawberries on top. Dust with cinnamon.
Spoon the yogurt over just before eating so the flakes stay crisp, and eat the egg alongside.
recipes.tip: Boil a few eggs on Sunday (they keep in the shell up to 7 days in the fridge) and toast a jar of seeds, and breakfast takes two minutes. Any ripe berry will do in place of the strawberries.

recipes.name: Huevos a la mexicana with black beans and orange
recipes.inspiredBy: Mexican huevos a la mexicana, with black beans and an orange on the side
recipes.about: Eggs scrambled with tomato, onion and fresh jalapeño, the red, white and green breakfast of a Mexican morning, with warm corn tortillas and black beans. The eggs and beans bring **iron and protein**, and the tomato, lime and a juicy orange on the side bring the vitamin C that helps you absorb the iron from the beans.
steps: Rinse the black beans and warm them in a small pot with the cumin and a splash of water, mashing about half with a fork, for 4 minutes. Keep them warm.
Wash the tomato, onion, jalapeño, cilantro and orange. Dice or chop the first four, and cut the orange into segments.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and soften the onion and jalapeño with a pinch of the salt for 3 minutes. Add the tomato and cook until the juices mostly cook off, about 3 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt, pour them in and stir gently until they are set with no liquid left, about 2 minutes. Squeeze over the lime and scatter the cilantro.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 30 seconds a side. Serve the eggs with the beans, the tortillas and the orange. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw eggs.
recipes.tip: Leave out the jalapeño for a milder plate and pass hot sauce at the table.

recipes.name: Tofu bhurji with peppers and spinach on whole-wheat toast
recipes.inspiredBy: North Indian paneer bhurji, with crumbled tofu in place of paneer
recipes.about: Crumbled tofu cooked with onion, ginger, green chili and red pepper in the style of a Punjabi paneer bhurji, with a handful of spinach wilted in and a squeeze of lemon, piled on whole-wheat toast. The tofu carries the **iron**, and the red pepper and lemon bring the vitamin C that helps you absorb it.
steps: Press the tofu between a few layers of paper towel for 5 minutes, then crumble it into small pieces with your hands.
Wash the pepper, spinach and cilantro. Dice the pepper, chop the spinach and cilantro, and chop the onion, ginger, garlic and chili.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the cumin and let it sizzle for 15 seconds, then add the onion and a pinch of the salt and cook until soft and golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Add the red pepper and cook 3 minutes, then stir in the turmeric, the crumbled tofu and the rest of the salt. Cook, stirring, until the tofu is hot and dry-looking with golden edges, about 5 minutes.
Fold in the spinach until it wilts, about 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat and finish with the garam masala, lemon juice and cilantro. Serve on the toast.
recipes.tip: Use a milder green pepper in place of the chili, or leave it out. Leftover bhurji also fills a warm whole-wheat pita.

recipes.name: Warm lentil salad with roasted red pepper, spinach and a boiled egg
recipes.inspiredBy: a French-style lentil salad, with roasted red pepper, spinach and an orange dressing
recipes.about: Tender lentils tossed warm with sweet roasted red pepper, spinach softened in the dressing and toasted pumpkin seeds, topped with a boiled egg and dressed with a light orange and lemon vinaigrette. The lentils bring **iron and protein**, and the pepper, orange and spinach bring the vitamin C that helps your body absorb it.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the pepper, toss the strips with half the oil and a pinch of the salt on a tray, and roast until soft and charred at the edges, about 20 minutes.
Lower the egg into a pot of gently boiling water and cook for 10 minutes until the yolk is firm. Cool it in cold water, then peel and halve it.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop, about 3 minutes. Wash the spinach and the orange.
Whisk the juice of half the orange with the lemon juice, the rest of the oil, the cumin and the rest of the salt. Cut the remaining orange into segments.
Rinse the lentils and warm them in a small pot with a splash of water until steaming, about 4 minutes. Drain well and toss with the dressing, the spinach and the onion so the spinach softens.
Fold in the roasted pepper and orange segments, top with the egg halves and seeds, and serve with the toast.
recipes.tip: It is just as good cold the next day; add the egg and seeds fresh.

recipes.name: Egg and chickpea pita with parsley, tomato and lemon-tahini
recipes.inspiredBy: Israeli sabich, with chickpeas and a boiled egg in the pita
recipes.about: A pita packed with garlicky chickpeas, sliced boiled egg, a big handful of parsley, tomato and crisp red pepper, drizzled with a lemony tahini dressing. The chickpeas and parsley bring **iron**, the egg and chickpeas bring protein, and the red pepper, tomato and lemon bring the vitamin C that helps you absorb it.
steps: Lower the egg into gently boiling water and cook for 10 minutes until the yolk is firm. Cool it in cold water, then peel and slice it.
Rinse the chickpeas well. Wash the parsley, tomato and red pepper, then chop the parsley and dice the tomato and pepper.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice, garlic and a pinch of the salt into a loose, tangy dressing, adding a spoonful of cold water only if it is too sharp.

Warm the olive oil in a small pan, stir in the cumin for 15 seconds and add the chickpeas and the rest of the salt. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and lightly golden, crushing a few with the back of a spoon.
Toss the chickpeas with the parsley, tomato, red pepper and onion. Warm the pita, split it open and stuff it with the salad and the egg slices. Drizzle with the tahini sauce.
recipes.tip: Warm the pita for a minute in a dry pan, or wrap it in a damp towel and microwave for 15 seconds.

recipes.name: Smashed sardines on rye with tomato, spinach and lemon
recipes.inspiredBy: Portuguese and Sicilian sardines on toast
recipes.about: Canned sardines mashed with lemon, parsley and onion, piled onto toasted rye with juicy tomato, baby spinach and strips of red pepper. Sardines are an **oily fish rich in omega-3, with iron**, and the lemon, tomato and pepper bring the vitamin C that helps you absorb it.
steps: Wash the tomato, spinach, pepper and parsley, then slice the tomato, cut the pepper into strips and chop the parsley.
Mash the sardines in a bowl with a fork, leaving some chunks, with the lemon juice, parsley, onion, half the olive oil and a grind of pepper.
Toast the rye until crisp. Drizzle the rest of the oil over it, then layer on the tomato slices and the spinach.
Pile the smashed sardines on top and serve the pepper strips alongside. Eat it straight away; the sardines are not a good leftover.
recipes.tip: A few capers or chopped olives are lovely in the sardine mix, but rinse them well since they are salty.

recipes.name: Beef and black bean chili over a baked potato
recipes.inspiredBy: Canadian-style beef chili, served over a baked potato
recipes.about: A smoky, deeply spiced chili of lean ground beef, black beans and tomatoes with plenty of red pepper, spooned over a baked potato and finished with lime and cilantro. The beef and beans bring **heme and plant iron together**, and the tomatoes, peppers and lime bring the vitamin C. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.

ingredients.note: whole canned tomatoes in juice, crushed by hand

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Prick the scrubbed potatoes with a fork and bake on a tray until very tender, about 50 minutes, while you make the chili.

Wash the pepper, cilantro and onion. Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and soften the onion and pepper with a pinch of the salt until golden at the edges, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.

Add the beef, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until no pink is left, about 6 minutes. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after the raw beef. Stir in the cumin, paprika, cinnamon and cayenne and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the crushed tomatoes with their juice, the rinsed beans, the rest of the salt and a splash of water. Simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes until thick. Check that the beef is cooked through, 71 °C (160 °F) on a thermometer.
Split the potatoes, spoon the chili over them and finish with the lime juice and cilantro.

Cool the second portion of chili in a shallow container within 2 hours, refrigerate and eat within 3 days. Reheat once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F), and bake or microwave a fresh potato to go with it.
recipes.tip: The chili freezes well for up to 3 months: cool it within 2 hours in a shallow container first, and freeze it without the potato. Thaw in the fridge overnight, eat within 2 days and never refreeze. Reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F). Short on time? Prick the potatoes and microwave them for 8 to 10 minutes, and the chili needs only about 35. A squeeze of lime on top brightens it.

recipes.name: Whole-wheat spaghetti with sardines, kale and apricot
recipes.inspiredBy: Sicilian pasta con le sarde, with kale and dried apricot in place of raisins
recipes.about: A quick take on Sicily's pasta con le sarde: sardines melted into garlic and olive oil with fennel seed, sweet dried apricot, kale and lemon, tossed through whole-wheat spaghetti. The sardines bring **omega-3**, and their soft bones add calcium, while the pasta and kale add iron and the lemon and kale bring the vitamin C.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil for the pasta. Wash the kale and parsley, slice the kale and the onion, and chop the apricot.

Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the fennel seed and onion with a pinch of the salt and cook until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, apricot and chili flakes for 1 minute.
Cook the spaghetti in the boiling water until just tender, about 10 minutes, adding the kale for the last 2 minutes. Save a cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Add the sardines to the pan and break them up with a spoon.
Toss in the pasta and kale with a splash of pasta water, the lemon juice and the rest of the salt until glossy, adding more pasta water if it looks dry. Heat until steaming hot.
Serve topped with the parsley. This is a one-sitting dish, not a leftover.
recipes.tip: Pasta con le sarde is traditionally finished with toasted breadcrumbs for crunch; a spoonful of coarse breadcrumbs fried in the pan works too.

recipes.name: Palak masoor dal with brown basmati
recipes.inspiredBy: North Indian dal palak, made with red lentils
recipes.about: A thick, golden red lentil dal with plenty of spinach, tomato, ginger and a sizzling cumin tadka, finished with lemon and served with nutty brown basmati rice. The lentils bring **plant iron**, with the spinach adding a little, and the tomato and lemon bring the vitamin C that helps you absorb it. It makes two portions.

ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

steps: Rinse the lentils and put them in a pot with the turmeric, a pinch of the salt and about three times their volume of water. Bring to the boil, skim off any foam, then simmer, partly covered, until soft and falling apart, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it in plenty of boiling water until tender, about 30 minutes. Drain and keep it covered.

Wash the spinach, tomato and cilantro. Warm the oil in a small pan, add the cumin and let it sizzle for 15 seconds, then add the onion and cook until golden, about 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger and cayenne for 1 minute.

Add the tomato and cook until it collapses, about 5 minutes. Stir this tadka into the lentils with the spinach and the rest of the salt and simmer until the spinach is soft and the dal is thick, about 5 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and finish with the garam masala, lemon juice and cilantro. Serve over the rice.
Cool the rice within 1 hour and the dal within 2 hours in shallow containers, refrigerate and eat within 3 days. Reheat once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
recipes.tip: Frozen spinach works if fresh is a hassle. The dal freezes well for up to 3 months: cool it within 2 hours first, freeze it without the rice and cook the rice fresh. Thaw in the fridge overnight, eat within 2 days and never refreeze. Reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F).

recipes.name: Mussels in tomato and paprika broth with kale and whole-wheat toast
recipes.inspiredBy: Spanish-style mussels steamed in tomato, garlic and smoked paprika
recipes.about: Mussels steamed open in a garlicky tomato and smoked paprika broth with kale softened in and a lot of parsley, with whole-wheat toast for mopping. Mussels are one of the best **iron-rich seafoods**, and the tomatoes, parsley and a squeeze of lemon bring the vitamin C that helps you absorb it. It is ready in about 40 minutes.

ingredients.note: shelled weight; buy them in the shell, about 3 to 4 times this weight
whole canned tomatoes in juice, crushed by hand

steps: Buy live mussels from a seller who keeps them on ice: the shells should be closed, or snap shut when tapped, and smell of the sea. Use them within 1 day of buying, 2 at most. Wash the kale and parsley, and slice the kale. Scrub them under cold running water and pull off the beards. Farmed mussels only need a scrub; if they feel gritty, soak them for 20 minutes in cold, lightly salted water, never fresh water. Throw away any that are cracked, that stay open when tapped, or that smell off. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after the raw mussels.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat and soften the onion with a pinch of the salt for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and chili flakes for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes with their juice, the kale and a splash of water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the kale is tender and the sauce is slightly thickened.

Add the mussels, cover tightly and steam over medium-high heat, shaking the pot once or twice, until the shells open, about 5 minutes. Throw away any that stay closed. Shellfish is safe at 74 °C (165 °F); in practice the shells are wide open and the flesh is firm, so give them one more minute after they open.

Stir in the lemon juice and most of the parsley. Ladle into a bowl, leaving any sandy liquid at the bottom of the pot, scatter over the rest of the parsley and serve with the toast. Eat it fresh; shellfish is not a good leftover.
recipes.tip: Keep mussels in the fridge in an open bowl covered with a damp cloth, never in a sealed bag or in fresh water, and cook them the day you buy them, or the next day at the latest.

recipes.name: Tofu and broccoli stir-fry with red pepper and cashews
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese-style tofu and broccoli stir-fry, with brown rice
recipes.about: Golden tofu with crisp broccoli and red pepper in a garlicky ginger, soy and lemon sauce, finished with toasted cashews and served over brown rice. The tofu and cashews bring **iron**, and the broccoli and red pepper bring plenty of vitamin C to help you absorb it. It makes two portions.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in plenty of boiling water until tender, about 30 minutes. Drain and keep it covered.
Press the tofu between paper towels for 10 minutes, then cut it into cubes. Wash the broccoli and pepper, then cut them up.
Whisk the soy sauce and lemon juice with a splash of water in a small bowl.
Warm half the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning once or twice, until golden on most sides, about 8 minutes. Lift it out.
Add the rest of the oil, then the broccoli with a splash of water, cover and steam for 2 minutes. Add the pepper and stir-fry 2 minutes, then the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return the tofu, pour in the sauce and toss until the tofu and vegetables are coated, about 1 minute. Scatter over the cashews and serve over the rice.
Cool the rice within 1 hour and the stir-fry within 2 hours, refrigerate in shallow containers and eat within 3 days. Reheat once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Toast the cashews in a dry pan for 3 minutes first for more flavour, and a teaspoon of toasted sesame oil on the rice is lovely.

recipes.name: Slow lamb, chickpea and apricot stew with spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: a Moroccan-style lamb tagine with apricots and chickpeas
recipes.about: A fragrant weekend stew of lean lamb leg simmered with cumin, ginger and cinnamon, chickpeas, carrots, dried apricots and tomatoes, with spinach wilted in at the end and brown rice on the side. The lamb is a **source of iron your body absorbs easily**, and the tomatoes, lemon and parsley bring the vitamin C. It makes two portions.

ingredients.note: lean leg, trimmed of visible fat and cut into cubes
whole canned tomatoes in juice, crushed by hand

steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Wash the spinach, carrots and parsley, and peel the carrots. Pat the lamb dry and season with the paprika, cumin and half the salt.
Warm the oil in a heavy ovenproof pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb in batches, about 5 minutes a batch. Lift it out. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after the raw lamb.
Lower the heat, add the onion and a pinch of the salt and cook until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cinnamon and turmeric for 1 minute.

Return the lamb with the carrots, the crushed tomatoes and their juice, the apricots and enough water to just cover. Bring to a simmer, cover and braise in the oven until the lamb is very tender, about 75 minutes. The lamb is cooked through at 71 °C (160 °F), well before it is tender.

Stir in the chickpeas and the rest of the salt and simmer, uncovered, on the stovetop for 10 minutes. Meanwhile cook the rinsed rice in plenty of boiling water until tender, about 30 minutes, and drain.
Stir the spinach into the stew until it wilts, about 1 minute. Finish with the lemon juice and parsley and serve over the rice.
Cool the rice within 1 hour and the stew within 2 hours in shallow containers, refrigerate and eat within 3 days. Reheat once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: A pressure cooker does the braise in 30 minutes. Ask the butcher for leg steaks and cube them yourself to keep it lean. The stew freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight, eat within 2 days and never refreeze; cool the rice and the stew first (1 hour for rice, 2 hours for the stew) before freezing, and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F).

recipes.name: Pan-seared mackerel on warm lentils with garlicky kale and parsley salsa verde
recipes.inspiredBy: Italian salsa verde over mackerel and lentils
recipes.about: Crisp-skinned Atlantic mackerel on warm lentils with garlicky kale, sweet roasted red pepper and a bright parsley and lemon salsa verde. Mackerel is an **oily fish with omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the lentils bring plant iron, with the kale, peppers and lemon bringing plenty of vitamin C alongside.

ingredients.note: fillets, skin on, pin bones removed

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the peppers, kale and parsley. Toss the pepper strips with a third of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a tray and roast until soft and charred at the edges, about 20 minutes.
For the salsa verde, stir the parsley, garlic, lemon juice, chili flakes, half the remaining oil and a pinch of salt together in a bowl and leave to sit for 10 minutes.

Warm the rinsed lentils in a small pot with the onion, a splash of water and a pinch of the salt until steaming, about 5 minutes. Cook the kale in a covered pan with a splash of water and a little of the garlic from the salsa until tender and bright, about 6 minutes.

Pat the mackerel dry and season with the paprika and the rest of the salt. Heat the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the fillets skin side down, pressing gently, until the skin is crisp, about 4 minutes. Flip and cook 2 minutes more, until the flesh flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and board after the raw fish.
Spoon the lentils and kale onto a plate, lay the mackerel on top, add the peppers and spoon over the salsa verde.
recipes.tip: Salsa verde keeps for 2 days in the fridge but loses its colour; make it fresh when you can.

recipes.name: Yogurt with strawberries, pumpkin seeds and ground flax
recipes.about: Thick plain Greek yogurt with sliced strawberries, a crunch of pumpkin seeds and a spoonful of ground flax. Dairy sits at a snack, away from the big iron meals, and the strawberries bring **vitamin C along with the seeds' iron**.
steps: Rinse the strawberries, then hull and slice them.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the strawberries and scatter over the pumpkin seeds and flax.

recipes.name: Smoky roasted chickpeas with an orange
recipes.about: Crunchy chickpeas roasted with smoked paprika and cumin, with a juicy orange on the side. The chickpeas bring **iron and fibre**, and the orange brings the vitamin C that helps you absorb it.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Rinse the chickpeas and pat them very dry with a towel.
Toss them on a tray with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt and roast, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp, about 25 minutes. Let them cool a few minutes to crisp up further.
Wash the orange, cut it into wedges and serve with the chickpeas. Keep leftovers in an open container; they soften in a day.

recipes.name: Dark chocolate with strawberries
recipes.about: A few squares of dark chocolate with a bowl of strawberries. Dark chocolate brings a little **iron** along with its flavour, and the strawberries bring vitamin C. It is a treat that happens to be useful.
steps: Rinse the strawberries.
Break the chocolate into squares and eat with the berries.

recipes.name: Dried apricots and cashews with an orange
recipes.about: Chewy dried apricots, creamy cashews and juicy orange wedges. The apricots and cashews bring **iron and copper**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges.
Serve the apricots, cashews and orange together in a small bowl.

recipes.name: Tahini hummus with red pepper sticks
recipes.about: A quick lemony hummus whirled from chickpeas and tahini, for dunking raw red pepper sticks. The chickpeas and tahini bring **iron and fibre**, and the red pepper brings plenty of vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pepper and cut it into sticks.
Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin, salt and a splash of cold water until very smooth, about 2 minutes. Add more water for a looser texture.
Serve the hummus with the pepper sticks. Keep any extra in the fridge for up to 3 days.
recipes.tip: A mini chopper or a stick blender in a tall jar copes with this small amount, or make a bigger batch and keep it up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Orange and strawberry cup with toasted pumpkin seeds
recipes.about: Juicy orange segments and strawberries with a handful of toasted pumpkin seeds for crunch. The seeds bring **iron and zinc**, and the fruit brings plenty of vitamin C.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop, about 3 minutes.
Wash the orange and strawberries. Cut the orange into segments and slice the strawberries, then scatter the warm seeds on top.

recipes.name: Orange yogurt with crunchy bran flakes
recipes.about: Thick plain yogurt with orange segments and a handful of crushed fortified bran flakes for crunch. The orange brings **vitamin C**, and the cereal brings a little iron. It keeps the dairy at a snack, apart from the bigger iron meals.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into segments.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the orange and scatter over the bran flakes just before eating.

recipes.name: Smoky lime pumpkin seeds and cashews
recipes.about: A warm, savoury mix of pumpkin seeds and cashews toasted in a dry pan with smoked paprika and finished with lime. The nuts and seeds bring **a little iron**, with magnesium and copper, and the lime brings a little vitamin C.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds and cashews in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until golden and fragrant, about 4 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, toss with the paprika, salt and lime juice, and let cool a few minutes. Eat warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Yogurt with chopped apricot, cashews and orange
recipes.about: Thick plain yogurt with chopped dried apricots, a few cashews and orange segments. It keeps the dairy at a snack, apart from the bigger iron meals, with **vitamin C from the orange** and a little iron from the apricots and cashews.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into segments.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the orange, apricots and cashews.
